name: bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity
claim: The v1 collagen IV network's ~zero elastic modulus is a rigidity-percolation effect: with NC1×1 + 7S×3 connectivity the mean coordination z ≤ 3 stays below the 2D central-force isostatic point z = 4, so raising crosslink connectivity alone cannot rigidify it — a measurable modulus needs junction bending (or true bundling bonds).
experiment: Sweep the max crosslinks per end (a bundling proxy: NC1×k + 7S×m, k,m rising) so the mean coordination z climbs, and measure the seed-ensemble elastic modulus vs z against the z = 4 threshold.
result: Across the achievable range z rises 1.24 → 3.72 (crosslinks 48 → 543 on 200 rods) but NEVER reaches z = 4, and the modulus stays statistically consistent with zero at every rung (−0.05 to −0.08 ± ~0.08–0.17 LJ, all CIs span 0). The NC1/7S topology saturates geometrically below the isostatic point, so central- force crosslinks cannot rigidify the sheet. Rigidity must come from junction bending — the "soft angles where rods join" the spec names.

purpose.question: Can more crosslink connectivity rigidify the v1 network, or is bending required?
purpose.mechanism: Maxwell rigidity percolation: a central-force network is floppy below z = 2d (= 4 in 2D). Bond-bending constraints lower the threshold and rigidify sub- isostatic networks.
purpose.expected_outcome: Modulus stays ~0 while z < 4; since NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at 3, connectivity alone never rigidifies — bending does.

key_assumptions: Mean coordination z = 1 + n_crosslinks/n_rods (beads = 2·n_rods; bonds = intra + crosslinks).
Raising NC1/7S max crosslinks is a proxy for lateral bundling (more junctions).
Same clean-room parameters and force-independent off-rate as stage 1.

findings.statement: Raising NC1/7S crosslinks lifts z to only ~3.7 (never 4), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 sheet.

expected.range: rigid only for z ≥ 4 (2D central-force isostatic point)

findings.explanation: NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at 3; bundling raises it but the geometry saturates below 4.
findings.next_action: implement junction bending (fix bond/create atype + angle_style) — the load-bearing v2 fix

config.title: Rigidity sweep — modulus vs coordination z

limitations: Bundling is modelled only as raised crosslink caps, not explicit lateral-association bonds.
Junction bending is NOT yet implemented — this study motivates it, does not test it.
Same LJ-unit / energy-scale caveat as stage 1.

report.title: Stage v3 — rigidity percolation: why the modulus is ~0
report.verdict: Central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 network: z tops out at ~3.7 (< 4) and the modulus is consistent with zero at every rung. Rigidity requires junction bending / bundling, not more crosslinks — a concrete, testable next step.
report.main_insight: The basement membrane's stiffness is a bending/bundling property, not a crosslink-count property — the constraint the AICS vertex-model coupling must respect.

sources.note: The two-bead-rod + stochastic-crosslink model; its ≈0.03 Pa modulus is the near-floppy regime this study explains.
